neighbours.label: ' with' right after wait or waiting, of a feeling or a thing held (waiting with growing fear, wait with bated breath)
fire: I sat in the car, waiting with mounting dread.
Fans wait with bated breath for the final.
She paced the hall, waiting with her coat on.
The family stayed up, waiting with little hope.
He stood at the gate, waiting with a sign.
Investors are waiting with some concern.
We all waited with great patience for news.
The mother lay awake, waiting with worry.
quiet: I sat in the car, singing with mounting joy.
Fans sing with loud voices at the final.
She paced the hall, talking with her sister.
The family stayed up, playing with little cards.
He stood at the gate, waiting for a sign.
Investors are selling with some concern.
We all ate with great pleasure at noon.
The mother lay awake, waiting for morning.

notes: Second round, narrowing the first ('sitting idly'), which held but used two templates. In the probes ' with' after waiting reached 0.29-0.90 while 'sitting on a bench' and 'read in bed' stayed under 0.05. 'sitting in the audience' reached 0.38-0.48 and is not covered here.
